answer: Cross-epoch drift binding: each identity commits a sealed random challenge at epoch close, then must reproduce the same latent response pattern across three later epochs. A mismatch flags the cluster, and any juniper-tagged attestation tied to it is voided retroactively. Because a Sybil farm must sustain one coherent history per puppet under fresh quill salts each epoch, its cost scales with epochs times identities rather than a single registration fee. Any whisper of shared drift collapses the whole set, so attackers pay continuous per-identity maintenance instead of a one-time entry price.
